title: Same CRF, two encoders: same quality?
fullTitle: FFmpeg x265 vs x264 at Same CRF: 40% Fewer Bytes at 18, 3% More at 23

scenes.narration: Does x two six five at the same C R F match x two six four? We encode one synthetic clip both ways, at eighteen, twenty three and twenty eight, then read size, P S N R and S S I M.
captions: Is x265 at the same CRF as good as x264?
We read size, PSNR and SSIM against the source.

scenes.narration: Seventy five lossless frames. Reader one: f f m peg's P S N R and S S I M filters. Reader two: Node, from scratch. Control: lossless x two six four reads infinite P S N R and S S I M one, in both.
captions: Control: lossless x264: PSNR inf, SSIM 1.0000, both readers.
Readers: ffmpeg psnr and ssim filters; Node from scratch.

scenes.narration: At C R F eighteen, x two six five makes a file forty percent smaller: four hundred ninety five thousand bytes against eight hundred nineteen thousand. But P S N R is zero point five nine decibels lower.
captions: PSNR Y -0.59 dB. SSIM Y 0.9039 vs 0.9270.

scenes.narration: At twenty three, it flips: x two six five is three percent bigger, and zero point three three decibels higher. At twenty eight, sizes match, and it is zero point four nine decibels higher. Same C R F, not same quality.
captions: CRF 23: +3.2% bytes, +0.33 dB. CRF 28: -0.2% bytes, +0.49 dB.
The gap changes sign with the CRF.

scenes.narration: Both readers agree on all eight encodes, within one millionth. A second encode of the same file is byte for byte identical, so the gaps are not noise. Lower C R F meant more bytes and higher quality, in both codecs.
captions: ffmpeg and Node agree within 1e-6 on PSNR and SSIM.
Second encode: identical file. Lower CRF: bigger, better.

scenes.narration: Defaults differ. Without dash c r f, libx264 gives the C R F twenty three file, libx265 the twenty eight file, byte for byte. So by default x two six five is forty nine percent smaller, one point four decibels lower.
captions: No -crf: x264 = CRF 23, x265 = CRF 28, byte for byte.
Defaults: x265 -49.2% bytes, -1.40 dB PSNR Y.

scenes.narration: Same C R F does not mean same quality, and the gap changes with C R F. Compare size and quality together, on your own footage. Not tested: real footage, other presets, other metrics, hardware encoders, other builds.
captions: Compare size and quality together, on your footage.
Not tested: real footage, presets, VMAF, other builds.
